chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about a man who repeats the prayer, does he repeat the Adhan and the Iqamah? He said, 'Yes.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the missed voluntary prayers (Nawafil) are made up at any time, provided it is not the time of a obligatory prayer (Fard), or at the rising of the sun, or at its setting. And it is disliked to make up voluntary prayers when the sun turns yellow (before sunset) until it sets. What has preceded previously contains a full explanation of what indicates this, and what increases that clarity is what he narrated:

key_terms.إِصْفَارُ الشَّمْسِ: Yellowing of the sun (time of dislike for prayer before sunset)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: Iqamah (Second call to prayer, immediately preceding prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating the Adhan and Iqamah when repeating a prayer, and when can missed voluntary prayers be made up?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the jurist clarifies that repeating the Adhan and Iqamah is obligatory when a prayer is repeated due to doubt or error, emphasizing the ritual completeness of the act. The text further delineates the jurisprudence of making up missed voluntary prayers (Qada al-Nawafil), permitting them at all times except during specific prohibited or disliked intervals such as sunrise, sunset, and the yellowing of the sun before Maghrib. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on maintaining the spiritual rhythm of worship while adhering to the cosmic timings of creation.
